text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes often develop slowly over years and can be very mild, including increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Frequent urination: Needing to pee more often, especially at night, because your kidneys try to remove extra sugar.
Increased thirst: Feeling very thirsty and having a dry mouth due to fluid loss from frequent urination.
Constant fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or weak because your body's cells cannot properly absorb glucose for energy.
Blurred vision: Experiencing blurry eyesight when high blood sugar causes the lenses in your eyes to swell.
Increased hunger: Feeling hungry soon after eating because energy is not reaching your cells.
Slow-healing sores: Noticing that cuts, scrapes, or bruises take a long time to heal.
Frequent infections: Getting recurring skin, yeast, or urinary tract infections because high sugar helps bacteria thrive.
Darkened skin patches: Developing dark, velvety patches in skin folds like the neck or armpits (acanthosis nigricans), which signal insulin resistance.
Tingling or numbness: Feeling a prickling sensation or numbness in your hands or feet from early nerve irritation.
